name: Vansen ArcGuard Insulated Shock-Resist Glove
description:
High-voltage insulation gloves used by electrical systems crews, transit infrastructure maintenance, and unlicensed grid tappers alike. Outer shell is matte industrial yellow with black hazard banding at the cuff — sun-faded on most working pairs to a pale mustard. The triple-layer construction sandwiches a dielectric rubber core between abrasion-resistant syn-textile inner and outer layers.

Knuckle and palm zones are thickened for mechanical protection. The extended gauntlet cuff seals with a rolled-bead edge that mates with standard insulated coverall sleeves. A small embossed voltage rating stamp on the wrist reads 40kV — though street-market versions often have the rating faked upward.
functionality: Rated 40kV dielectric insulation (genuine units). Mechanical impact resistance at knuckle and palm. Rolled-bead cuff seals against insulated coverall sleeves. Resists tearing from cable handling and conduit work.
what_it_says: You work inside the city's nervous system and you know exactly how badly it can hurt you.
story_hooks: A maintenance worker is found unconscious near a junction box — their Vansen ArcGuards were genuine, but something punched through the dielectric layer deliberately.
A street vendor is moving counterfeit ArcGuards with faked 80kV stamps; three grid tappers have already been hospitalized and none of them reported it.
A pair of these gloves is the only item recovered from a flooded Tier 1 transformer vault — the worker's name is stenciled inside, but they were declared dead six months ago.
